nodes.title: Types of Solutions & Henry's Law
points: Solution: Homogeneous mixture of two or more chemically non-reacting substances. Binary solution = 1 solute + 1 solvent.
Solubility: Maximum amount of solute dissolved in 100 g of solvent at specified temperature.
Henry's Law: The solubility (S) of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the pressure (P) of the gas over the solution: S = K_H · P.
Units of K_H: mol L⁻¹ bar⁻¹ or mol dm⁻³ bar⁻¹.
Temperature Effect: Solubility of a gas in a liquid DECREASES with increasing temperature (dissolution is exothermic: Gas + Solvent ⇌ Solution + Heat).
Exceptions to Henry's Law: Gases like NH₃ and HCl which react chemically with water or ionize do not obey Henry's law.

nodes.title: Raoult's Law & Vapor Pressure of Liquid Solutions
points: Raoult's Law for Volatile Liquids: For any volatile component, partial vapor pressure is directly proportional to its mole fraction: P₁ = P₁° x₁ and P₂ = P₂° x₂.
Total Vapor Pressure: P_total = P₁ + P₂ = P₁° x₁ + P₂° x₂ = P₁° + (P₂° − P₁°) x₂.
Vapor Phase Composition (Dalton's Law): y₁ = P₁ / P_total and y₂ = P₂ / P_total.
Vapor pressure of a liquid increases with temperature and decreases when a non-volatile solute is added.

nodes.title: Ideal vs Non-Ideal Solutions & Deviations
points: Ideal Solutions: Obey Raoult's law at all concentrations and temperatures. ΔH_mix = 0, ΔV_mix = 0. Intermolecular forces A-B equal A-A and B-B (e.g., Benzene + Toluene, n-Hexane + n-Heptane, Bromoethane + Chloroethane).

Non-Ideal Solutions with POSITIVE Deviation: P_total > Raoult's prediction. A-B interactions are WEAKER than A-A and B-B. ΔH_mix > 0 (endothermic), ΔV_mix > 0 (expansion). Form MINIMUM boiling azeotropes (e.g., Ethanol + Acetone, Carbon disulfide + Acetone).

Non-Ideal Solutions with NEGATIVE Deviation: P_total < Raoult's prediction. A-B interactions are STRONGER than A-A and B-B (new H-bonding). ΔH_mix < 0 (exothermic), ΔV_mix < 0 (contraction). Form MAXIMUM boiling azeotropes (e.g., Chloroform + Acetone, Phenol + Aniline, HNO₃ + Water).

nodes.title: Colligative Property 1: Relative Lowering of Vapor Pressure (RLVP)
points: Colligative Properties: Properties that depend solely on the NUMBER of solute particles, not on their chemical identity.
Vapor Pressure Lowering: ΔP = P₁° − P = P₁° x₂.
Relative Lowering of Vapor Pressure (RLVP): (P₁° − P) / P₁° = x₂ (mole fraction of non-volatile solute).
For dilute solutions: x₂ ≈ n₂ / n₁ = (W₂ · M₁) / (M₂ · W₁).
Molar Mass of Solute (M₂): M₂ = (W₂ · M₁ · P₁°) / (ΔP · W₁).

nodes.title: Colligative Property 2: Elevation of Boiling Point (ΔT_b)
points: Boiling Point: Temperature at which vapor pressure of liquid equals atmospheric pressure.
Elevation of Boiling Point: ΔT_b = T_b − T_b° (where T_b is solution boiling point, T_b° is pure solvent).
Relationship with Molality: ΔT_b = K_b · m, where K_b is Ebullioscopic Constant (Molal Elevation Constant).
SI Unit of K_b: K kg mol⁻¹.
Molar Mass of Solute: M₂ = (1000 · K_b · W₂) / (ΔT_b · W₁).

nodes.title: Colligative Property 3: Depression of Freezing Point (ΔT_f)
points: Freezing Point: Temperature at which vapor pressure of liquid equals vapor pressure of solid solvent.
Depression of Freezing Point: ΔT_f = T_f° − T_f (where T_f° is pure solvent, T_f is solution).
Relationship with Molality: ΔT_f = K_f · m, where K_f is Cryoscopic Constant (Molal Depression Constant).
SI Unit of K_f: K kg mol⁻¹.
Molar Mass of Solute: M₂ = (1000 · K_f · W₂) / (ΔT_f · W₁).
Antifreeze Application: Ethylene glycol added to automobile radiator water lowers freezing point in winter.

nodes.title: Colligative Property 4: Osmotic Pressure (π) & Reverse Osmosis
points: Osmosis: Spontaneous flow of solvent molecules into a solution through a Semi-Permeable Membrane (SPM).
Osmotic Pressure (π): Minimum excess hydrostatic pressure that must be applied to the solution to prevent osmosis.
van 't Hoff Equation: π = C R T = (n₂ / V) R T = (W₂ · R · T) / (M₂ · V).
Types of Solutions based on π:
1. Isotonic: π₁ = π₂ (same osmotic pressure, no net osmosis).
2. Hypertonic: Solution with higher osmotic pressure (cell shrinks / plasmolysis).
3. Hypotonic: Solution with lower osmotic pressure (cell swells and bursts).

Reverse Osmosis (RO): Applying pressure greater than osmotic pressure (P > π) on solution side forces solvent through SPM from solution to pure water (desalination of seawater, cellulose acetate membrane).

formulas.label: Osmotic pressure
formulas.expr: π = C R T = (W₂ R T) / (M₂ V)

nodes.title: Abnormal Molar Masses & van 't Hoff Factor (i)
points: van 't Hoff Factor (i): Measures the extent of dissociation or association of solute in solution:
i = (Observed colligative property) / (Theoretical colligative property) = M_theoretical / M_observed.
i = Total moles of particles after dissociation or association / Initial moles of particles.
1. For Dissociation (Electrolytes, e.g., NaCl, CaCl₂): i > 1 ⟹ M_observed < M_theoretical.
Degree of Dissociation (α): α = (i − 1) / (n' − 1), where n' is number of ions produced per formula unit.
2. For Association (e.g., Benzoic acid in benzene dimers): i < 1 ⟹ M_observed > M_theoretical.
Degree of Association (α): α = (1 − i) / (1 − 1/n').
Modified Colligative Equations: ΔP/P₁° = i x₂; ΔT_b = i K_b m; ΔT_f = i K_f m; π = i C R T.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Derivations & Graphs
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive relationship between elevation of boiling point (ΔT_b) and molar mass of solute (M₂).
Board Favourite #2: Derive relationship between depression of freezing point (ΔT_f) and molar mass of solute (M₂).
Board Favourite #3: State Raoult's law and derive expression for relative lowering of vapor pressure.
Board Favourite #4: Derive relation between van 't Hoff factor (i) and degree of dissociation (α).
Board Favourite #5: Sketch and label vapor pressure vs temperature curves for: (1) Boiling point elevation, (2) Freezing point depression.

formulas.label: Boiling derivation
formulas.expr: ΔT_b ∝ m ⟹ ΔT_b = K_b [1000 W₂ / (M₂ W₁)]

nodes.title: MHT-CET Colligative Traps, Osmotic Hacks & Ranking Tricks
points: Colligative Value Ranking Shortcut: For equimolar solutions, the value of colligative property (ΔT_b, ΔT_f, π, RLVP) is directly proportional to i:
Order: 0.1 M Al₂(SO₄)₃ (i = 5) > 0.1 M BaCl₂ (i = 3) > 0.1 M NaCl (i = 2) > 0.1 M Urea / Glucose (i = 1).
Freezing Point Trap: Highest ΔT_f means LOWEST freezing point T_f! (Solution with highest i freezes at the lowest temperature).
Boiling Point Trap: Highest ΔT_b means HIGHEST boiling point T_b!

Why Osmotic Pressure is Preferred for Biomolecules: (1) Measurable at room temperature (proteins denature at high T), (2) Uses molarity instead of molality, (3) Magnitude is large and easily readable even for dilute solutions.

formulas.label: Lowest freezing point rule
formulas.expr: T_f = T_f° − i K_f m (Max i ⟹ Lowest T_f)

formulas.label: Highest boiling point rule
formulas.expr: T_b = T_b° + i K_b m (Max i ⟹ Highest T_b)
